page.overview:
Who is David Ferrer?

David Ferrer was a French historic racing driver and enthusiast who participated in various classic motorsport events across Europe. He gained posthumous recognition after being fatally injured during the 2017 Monaco Historic Grand Prix, one of the most prestigious events for vintage race cars. Ferrer was a well-regarded member of the historic motorsport community, known for his passion for racing and his carefully maintained vintage machines.

David Ferrer competed primarily in historic racing categories, often driving vintage Formula 1 and Formula 2 cars from the 1960s and 1970s. These events celebrate the heritage of motorsport and are typically contested by wealthy amateurs, collectors, and former professionals. Ferrer was a regular entrant in European historic series and was respected for both his driving ability and mechanical understanding of classic racing machinery.

On May 13, 2017, David Ferrer was competing in the Serie C race at the Monaco Historic Grand Prix, an event showcasing Formula 1 cars built between 1966 and 1972. He was driving a March 701, a Formula One car originally built in 1970 and famously driven by Jackie Stewart and Chris Amon.

During a practice session at the legendary Monte Carlo street circuit, Ferrer lost control of his car at Casino Square — one of the fastest and most challenging sections of the track. The vehicle struck the barriers at high speed and flipped, landing upside down. Emergency services responded quickly, and Ferrer was airlifted to a hospital in Nice, France.
